title: Triage
description: The judged outcome of one run's survivors.

caveats.description:
Statements that must accompany any presentation of these classifications.
Written into the document rather than into a renderer, so that a reader who
only has the file still meets them.

dismissed.description:
The survivors a person had already dismissed, which were not asked about at
all. Listed rather than left out, because a reader comparing this document
with the run's report has to be able to account for every survivor in it.

entries.description: One entry per survivor, in the report's order.

judge.description: Who was asked about them, and what they were asked.

Claim.description:
What a model claimed about a mutation.

Any string is valid here. A consumer reads a value this contract version does not define as `unknown` rather than refusing the document that carries it, so a validator must not refuse it either. The values this version does define:
- `distinguishable` — It said there is an input for which the two versions do different things.
- `equivalent` — It said there is no such input.
- `unknown` — A claim this consumer does not know, written by a newer producer.

Classification.description:
What was established about a survivor.

Any string is valid here. A consumer reads a value this contract version does not define as `unknown` rather than refusing the document that carries it, so a validator must not refuse it either. The values this version does define:
- `distinguished_at_function_level` — One input was run against both versions of the function and they did different things. Whether the program can reach that input is unverified.
- `suspected_equivalent` — A model said the mutation changes nothing, and nothing was run to check it.
- `undecided` — No comparison was made. `undecided` says why.
- `unknown` — A classification this consumer does not know, written by a newer producer.

DismissalReason.description:
Why a mutation was dismissed.

Two reasons, and the difference between them is worth keeping: one says the
mutation could not have been caught by any test, and the other says it could and
that a test for it would not be worth having. Only the second is a statement
about what the project wants.

Any string is valid here. A consumer reads a value this contract version does not define as `unknown` rather than refusing the document that carries it, so a validator must not refuse it either. The values this version does define:
- `equivalent` — It cannot change what the program does, so no test could have caught it.
- `not_useful` — It can, and a test pinning that is not one this project wants.
- `unknown` — A reason this consumer does not know, written by a newer producer.

Dismissed.description: One survivor that was not judged, because a person had already dismissed it.

dismissed_at.description: When they did, RFC 3339, as the suppression records it.

file.description: Target file, POSIX-style and relative to the project root.

mutant_id.description: The manifest mutant this is about.

Ending.description:
How a call ended.

Any string is valid here. A consumer reads a value this contract version does not define as `unknown` rather than refusing the document that carries it, so a validator must not refuse it either. The values this version does define:
- `returned` — It returned a value.
- `raised` — It raised an exception.
- `unknown` — An ending this consumer does not know, reported by a newer pack.

Judge.description: Who was asked, and what they were asked.

model.description: The model that was asked, as the caller named it.

model_resolved.description: The model that answered, as it named itself. Absent when none did.

prompt_version.description:
Which revision of the judging prompt was sent. A change in how survivors
sort is traceable to a change in what was asked only if this is recorded.

Observation.description:
What one version of the function did with the witness call.

Every field of it is the agreed account of several runs: a side that produced
two different accounts is reported as nondeterministic instead, and never
arrives here.

message.description:
The exception's own message, with no traceback in it: a traceback carries
line numbers, and the two versions have different line numbers by
construction.

stdout.description:
Whatever the call wrote to standard output, captured and compared like any
other observable result.

type_name.description: The type of the returned value, or of the exception that was raised.

value.description:
The value it returned, rendered by the language's own means, or absent when
the call raised instead.

ProbeOutcome.description:
Whether one input told the two versions of a function apart.

Any string is valid here. A consumer reads a value this contract version does not define as `unknown` rather than refusing the document that carries it, so a validator must not refuse it either. The values this version does define:
- `differs` — The two versions did observably different things on this input.
- `indistinguishable` — They did the same thing on this input. Not a finding of equivalence: it is one input, and the claim it fails to support is a claim about all of them.
- `undecided` — No comparison could be made. `undecided` says why.
- `unknown` — An outcome this consumer does not know, reported by a newer pack.

ProbeReport.description: The result of running one witness call against both versions of a function.

call.description: The witness call, exactly as the caller wrote it.

file.description:
The file the function lives in, POSIX-style and relative to the root the
probe was pointed at. Echoed back so a caller can tell that the answer is
about the file it asked about.

mutant.description: What the mutated function did, on the same terms.

original.description:
What the unmutated function did. Absent when it was never observed
consistently enough to describe, which is what a nondeterministic side
means.

outcome.description: Whether the two versions did the same thing.

runs_per_side.description:
How many times each version was run, each time in a subprocess of its own.
More than one because a side that disagrees with itself cannot be compared
with anything.

undecided.description:
Why no comparison could be made. Present when, and only when, `outcome` is
`undecided`.

Span.description:
A half-open byte range over a file's raw bytes: `[start_byte, end_byte)`.
That `start_byte` is below `end_byte` is a validation rule, not a schema
constraint.

calls.description:
How many calls were made to the model, the failed ones included: a provider
charges for those too.

total_tokens.description: What the provider reported as the sum.

claim.description:
What the model claimed, when one answered. A record of the question, not
evidence for the classification.

detail.description:
One line for display, saying what happened in a person's terms. Not machine
readable: everything a machine reads is in the fields above.

file.description: Target file, POSIX-style and relative to the project root.

mutant_id.description: The manifest mutant this entry is about.

original.description: The text it replaces, as the manifest holds it.

probe.description: What happened when that input was run. Absent when none was run.

span.description: The byte range the mutation replaces.

undecided.description:
Why nothing was established. Present when, and only when, `classification`
is `undecided`.

witness.description:
The input the model offered, when it offered one. Kept whether or not it
turned out to separate anything, because a witness that did not is the most
useful thing a reader of this document can see.

TriageRun.description: The run this document is a second opinion on.

report.description:
The document whose survivors were judged, relative to the run directory.
Named rather than assumed: this is a claim about that document's verdicts,
and a reader has to be able to tell which one.

run_id.description: Identifier shared with the run directory, the results, and the report.

TriageScore.description: Aggregate counts over one triage. Every field is a plain count of `entries`.

distinguished_at_function_level.description: Those one input separated at the level of the function.

suspected_equivalent.description: Those a model called equivalent, unchecked.

Undecided.description:
Why nothing was established about a survivor.

Long, and every entry earns its place: what a person does next differs for each
of these, and collapsing them into one "unknown" would leave every reader
guessing which of them they had.

Any string is valid here. A consumer reads a value this contract version does not define as `unknown` rather than refusing the document that carries it, so a validator must not refuse it either. The values this version does define:
- `no_witness` — The model claimed a difference and named no input a probe could run.
- `witness_showed_no_difference` — The input it named was run, and the two versions did the same thing. This is **not** evidence of equivalence: one input failed to separate them, and the claim it fails to support was a claim about every input.
- `nondeterministic` — A version of the function did not agree with itself across its own runs.
- `incomparable` — A value came back that two processes cannot be said to agree about.
- `unsafe_witness` — The input was not one a probe evaluates: an argument that is not a literal.
- `method` — The name the input used is a method, which has no receiver a witness names.
- `no_such_function` — The module defines no function of that name, so there was nothing to run.
- `timed_out` — A version did not finish inside the time limit.
- `no_judgement` — No judgement could be obtained at all — the model, or the pack, could not answer about this survivor. The one reason here that is about the tools rather than about the mutation.
- `unknown` — A reason this consumer does not know, written by a newer producer.

Undecided2.description:
Why a probe could not compare the two versions.

Any string is valid here. A consumer reads a value this contract version does not define as `unknown` rather than refusing the document that carries it, so a validator must not refuse it either. The values this version does define:
- `nondeterministic` — One version did not agree with itself across its own runs, so there is nothing stable to compare the other version against.
- `incomparable` — A value came back whose type compares by identity rather than by content, so two of them made in two processes cannot be told equal or unequal.
- `unsafe_witness` — The call was not the form a probe evaluates: an argument that is not a literal, or anything else the whitelist refuses.
- `method` — The name the call uses is a method rather than a function of the module. A method needs a receiver, and nothing in a witness says what it should be.
- `no_such_function` — The module defines no function of that name at all, so there was nothing to run — which is a fact about the witness, not about the mutation.
- `timed_out` — One version did not finish inside the time limit, so what it would have done is unknown.
- `unknown` — A reason this consumer does not know, reported by a newer pack.

Witness.description: The input a model offered, as it offered it.

call.description: One call of the function, with literal arguments.

expect_mutant.description: What it expected the mutated function to do. Recorded, as above.

expect_original.description:
What the model expected the unmutated function to do with it.

Recorded and never compared against what happened. A prediction of a result
is not evidence about the result, and grading the prediction would be
grading the wrong thing — what the probe compares is the two results.
